children.translated_text: <s>Yamasmṛti</s>.
<s>Oṃ</s> <s>tatsad</s> — salutation to <s>Brahman</s>.
The <s>dharma</s> declared in <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>,
for the <s>varṇas</s> in due order,
was expounded, when asked by the sages,
by <s>Yama</s>, the foremost among munis.
He who, while eating or being impure,
touches a <s>caṇḍāla</s> or an outcaste,
whether out of anger or out of ignorance —
I shall declare the expiation for him.
He should observe a fast of six nights or three nights,
respectively, as prescribed;
having bathed at the three <s>savanas</s> (morning, midday, and evening pressings), a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>
is purified by <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five cow-products).
If, while a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is eating,
his bowel happens to discharge,
in the state of having leavings in the mouth or being impure,
one should prescribe the purification for him.
The twice-born should first perform purification,
and then sip water (<s>ācamana</s>);
having fasted for a day and a night,
he is purified by <s>pañcagavya</s>.
If one urinates while swallowing food,
or urinates after having eaten,
having fasted for a day and a night,
he should offer oblations of ghee into the fire.
When at mealtime a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>
happens to become impure,
placing that morsel on the ground
and bathing, he attains purity.
But if he has swallowed that morsel,
he is purified by a one-day fast;
and if he has eaten all of it,
he is purified by a three-night fast.
If while eating there is a purging of the bowels,
one who is unwell should recite three hundred times;
one who is well should recite three thousand times —
the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the supreme purifier.
A twice-born who is touched by <s>caṇḍālas</s> or <s>śvapacas</s>,
or who has excreted urine or feces in their presence,
should observe a three-night penance;
if he has eaten their leavings, he should observe six nights.
If an outcaste touches a menstruating woman
or a woman in her lying-in period,
purification is achieved by a three-night fast —
thus declared <s>Śātātapa</s>.
A menstruating woman who is touched
by dogs, elephants, crows, and the like,
should remain fasting and pure;
she is purified by the bath at the proper time.
When two menstruating women
happen to touch each other,
they are purified by <s>pañcagavya</s>
and additionally by <s>brahma-kūrca</s>.
If a menstruating woman is touched
by one who has food-leavings in the mouth,
she attains purification through a <s>kṛcchra</s> penance;
a <s>śūdra</s> woman, through charity and fasting.
When one is touched by a person who is not impure with food-leavings,
bathing is prescribed for him;
but one touched by a person with food-leavings
should perform a <s>prājāpatya</s> penance.
During the fertile season, bathing after intercourse
is prescribed, owing to the possibility of conception;
but having gone to a woman outside the fertile season,
the purification is the same as for urine and feces.
Both husband and wife become impure
when they have gone to bed together;
the woman who has risen from the bed
becomes pure, but the man remains impure.
A wife who, out of wickedness,
fails to render service to her husband's body,
should be punished for twelve years,
and abandoned without her property.
Those who abandon relatives who are not outcastes
should be fined the highest amercement (<s>uttamasāhasa</s>);
for a father may indeed become an outcaste,
but never a mother.
He who attempts to kill himself
by means of a rope and such devices —
if dead, he should be smeared with impure substances;
if alive, the fine is two hundred <s>paṇas</s>.
His sons and friends should be fined
one <s>paṇika</s> each;
and then they should perform <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation)
as enjoined by the <s>śāstra</s>.
Those who have been rescued from drowning, hanging,
or who have fallen from renunciation or a fast unto death,
or from poison, falling from a height, or near-fatal
weapon-wounds — those who have been struck down,
these nine who have turned back from suicide
are excluded from all social intercourse;
they are purified by a <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> penance
or by two <s>taptakṛcchra</s> penances.
A sinner who has attempted both ways
and fallen from the dark and the spotted cow vow,
is purified by two <s>cāndrāyaṇas</s>,
and by giving a cow and a bull.
One bitten by dogs, jackals, monkeys, and such animals,
or by humans — excluding sexual contact —
is immediately purified by bathing,
whether by day, at the <s>saṃdhyās</s> (twilight junctures), or at night.
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who unknowingly eats
the food of a <s>caṇḍāla</s>,
subsisting on cow-urine and barley gruel,
is purified in half a month.
One who has set fire to a cow-pen or a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s house,
or who finds a dead person hanged and the like,
and cuts the ropes — for that,
a twice-born should perform one <s>kṛcchra</s> penance.
Having eaten the food of <s>caṇḍālas</s> and <s>pukkasas</s>,
or having gone to their women,
one should perform a <s>kṛcchra</s> for one year if done knowingly;
if unknowingly, two <s>cāndrāyaṇas</s>.
For those who eat the food of <s>Kāpālikas</s>,
and likewise for those who go to their women,
one should perform a <s>kṛcchra</s> for one year if done knowingly;
if unknowingly, two <s>cāndrāyaṇas</s>.
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who approaches a forbidden woman,
or who consumes liquor, beef, or meat,
being enclosed by a <s>taptakṛcchra</s> penance
and wearing the <s>mauñjī</s> (muñja-grass girdle), is purified by a fire-offering.
The perpetrators of the four great sins (<s>mahāpātakas</s>),
without distinction,
are purified by entering fire,
or by standing in a great sacrificial rite.
Even for a secret transgression, a man
who practices it for a month,
is purified by the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa-sūkta</s>,
standing immersed in water.
A washerman, a leather-worker,
an actor, and a <s>buruḍa</s>,
a fisherman, a <s>meda</s>, and a <s>bhilla</s> —
these seven are known as outcastes (<s>antyajas</s>).
Having eaten their food, gone to their women,
drunk their water, or accepted gifts from them,
one should perform a <s>kṛcchra</s> for one year if done knowingly;
if unknowingly, two <s>cāndrāyaṇas</s>.
Having gone to one's mother, the teacher's wife,
one's sister, daughter, or daughter-in-law,
one should enter fire after approaching them;
no other purification is prescribed.
For approaching a queen, a female renunciant, a wet-nurse,
or a woman of a higher <s>varṇa</s>,
one should perform a double <s>kṛcchra</s>,
and also for approaching a woman of the same <s>gotra</s>.
For approaching women of one's father's <s>gotra</s>
or one's mother's <s>gotra</s>,
and for all cases of adultery,
one should perform the <s>sāṃtapana kṛcchra</s>.
The twice-born dispel the sin
of visiting a prostitute
by drinking once well-heated
<s>kuśa</s>-grass water for five nights.
Some prescribe the vow for violating the teacher's bed (<s>gurutalpa</s>),
some the vow for killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,
some prescribe the vow for cow-slaughter,
and some the vow for a <s>brahmacārin</s> who breaks his vow.
He who strikes a cow with a stick
with an upward blow and brings her down,
for him a double cow-penance
should be prescribed as <s>prāyaścitta</s>.
A stick as thick as a thumb
and one arm's length in measure,
moist and with leaves —
that is called the cow-stick (<s>godaṇḍa</s>).
If, when a cow is struck down,
the fetus also falls,
one should perform a <s>kṛcchra</s> for each one separately,
as before, so again.
One quarter of the penance when merely conceived,
two quarters when limbs have formed,
three-quarters of a <s>kṛcchra</s> is prescribed
for killing an unconscious fetus;
when the fetus is complete with all limbs and parts,
endowed with vital fluid,
one should perform a full <s>kṛcchra</s> for each —
this is the expiation for cow-slaughter.
In tying up, confining,
or injury from stones to cows,
if death results,
the one who caused it is not tainted.
If the cow, having fainted or fallen,
or having been struck by a stick,
gets up and walks six steps,
or seven, five, or ten,
or if she takes a morsel of food,
or if she drinks water,
for those that perish from a prior disease,
no <s>prāyaścitta</s> is prescribed.
If cows are killed by wood, clods of earth,
stones, or weapons,
what <s>prāyaścitta</s> applies in each case
is stated in the respective <s>śāstras</s>:
for wood, one should perform <s>sāṃtapana</s>;
for a clod, <s>prājāpatya</s>;
for a stone, <s>taptakṛcchra</s>;
and for a weapon, <s>atikṛcchra</s>.
When one gives medicine, oil, or food
to cows or <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
and calamity befalls while it is being given,
no <s>prāyaścitta</s> is prescribed.
In the administration of oil or medicinal drinks,
or in the consuming of medicines,
or in the extraction of foreign objects from wounds,
no <s>prāyaścitta</s> is prescribed.
For tying calves by the neck,
for medical treatment,
and for the purpose of herding them in the evening —
there is no fault in confining or tying.
At one quarter of the penance, only the body hair is shaved;
at two quarters, the beard alone;
at three quarters, all hair except the topknot;
at the full penance, everything should be shaved.
Having removed all the hair,
one should cut it to the length of two finger-breadths;
thus indeed for women,
cutting to this length is prescribed instead of full shaving.
A woman should not have her head shaved,
nor should she sit in the <s>vīrāsana</s> posture,
nor should she dwell in a cow-pen,
nor should she follow the cow on its wanderings.
For a king, a prince,
or a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,
one should prescribe <s>prāyaścitta</s>
without requiring them to shave.
For the sake of preserving the hair,
a double vow should be prescribed;
and when the double vow is performed,
the ritual fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) should also be doubled.
If the doubled fee is not given
while the hair is preserved,
the sin of the killer is not diminished,
and the one who prescribes the penance goes to hell.
Those who prescribe a <s>prāyaścitta</s>
not sanctioned by <s>Śruti</s> or <s>Smṛti</s>,
those obstructors of <s>dharma</s> —
the king should punish them with a fine.
If the king does not punish them,
being somehow deluded by desire,
that sin, multiplied a hundredfold,
descends upon him alone.
After the <s>prāyaścitta</s> has been performed,
one should feed <s>brāhmaṇas</s>;
and one should give twenty cows and a bull
as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee) to them.
When cows are brought down by worms born from wounds,
or by flies,
one should perform half a <s>kṛcchra</s>
and give <s>dakṣiṇā</s> according to one's ability.
Having performed the <s>prāyaścitta</s>
and having fed the best of twice-born,
one should give gold equal to one <s>āṣaka</s> (a small weight);
then purification is ordained.
When one is touched by <s>caṇḍālas</s> or <s>śvapacas</s> at night,
bathing is prescribed;
one should not stay there at night,
and is purified immediately by bathing.
But if one stays the night
unknowingly and without discernment,
then the sin from that contact
revolves a hundredfold.
When the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar asterisms) rise,
and the planets that are above,
when the water is touched by their rays,
one should perform bathing.
From walls, from water within ant-hills,
from rat-burrows and pathways,
from cremation grounds and from places where purification residue remains,
the seven types of earth should not be collected.
<s>Iṣṭāpūrta</s> (sacrificial and charitable merit) should be performed
by a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> with great effort.
Through <s>iṣṭa</s> (sacrifice) one obtains heaven;
through <s>pūrta</s> (charitable works) one attains liberation.
<s>Iṣṭa</s> (sacrifice) depends upon wealth;
a tank is said to be <s>pūrta</s> (meritorious work),
and gardens especially,
and likewise temple water-troughs.
Wells, step-wells, and tanks,
and temples of deities,
whoever restores those that have fallen into disrepair,
he obtains the fruit of <s>pūrta</s> (charitable merit).
One should collect urine from a white cow,
and dung from a black cow,
milk should be taken from a tawny cow,
and curd is prescribed from a white cow.
Ghee should be taken from a reddish-brown cow;
it destroys great sins.
At every <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford), in river water,
each substance separately with <s>kuśa</s> grass,
having gathered them with <s>praṇava</s> (the syllable Oṃ) indeed,
and having raised them with <s>praṇava</s>,
having stirred them with <s>praṇava</s>,
one should drink them with <s>praṇava</s>.
In the middle leaf of a <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) tree,
or in a copper vessel,
one should drink from a lotus leaf, or
from a copper or an auspicious earthen vessel.
When a birth-impurity has arisen,
and a second one occurs,
in the second there is no fault;
purification comes by the first alone.
The birth-impurity is purified by the birth itself;
likewise death-impurity by the death itself.
In the case of miscarriage, according to the month,
three days should be prescribed.
By nights equal in number to the months of pregnancy,
purification from miscarriage is achieved.
A virtuous woman, when her menstrual period has ceased,
a menstruating woman is purified by bathing.
A woman separates from her natal <s>gotra</s> (lineage)
at the seventh step of marriage.
With the husband's <s>gotra</s>, the rites of
<s>piṇḍa</s> (ancestral offering) and water-offering should be performed for her.
Two <s>piṇḍas</s> (ancestral offerings) should be given for the father;
in each <s>piṇḍa</s>, two names are invoked.
Three <s>piṇḍas</s> should be given for six persons;
thus the giver is not confused.
The mother partakes of the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite) together with her own husband,
having eaten with the deity.
The paternal grandmother likewise with her own husband,
and the great-grandmother with her own.
Year after year one should perform
the honoring of one's mother and father.
One should feed at the <s>śrāddha</s> without a deity-portion,
and offer a single <s>piṇḍa</s>.
The regular, the occasional, the desire-fulfilling,
and the <s>vṛddhiśrāddha</s> (joyous ancestral rite),
and the <s>pārvaṇa</s> (fortnightly rite) -- these should be known
as five types of <s>śrāddha</s> by the wise.
During an eclipse of a planet, at the <s>saṃkrānti</s> (solstice/equinox),
at festival days, great occasions, and <s>mahālaya</s> (ancestral fortnight),
a man should offer three <s>piṇḍas</s>,
but only one on the day of death.
An unmarried girl is not separate
in <s>piṇḍa</s>, <s>gotra</s>, or birth-impurity.
By the two mantras of <s>pāṇigrahaṇa</s> (the marriage hand-clasping),
she then separates from her natal <s>gotra</s>.
By whichever <s>varṇa</s> (social class)
a girl is married,
she shares the same birth-impurity as that family,
and likewise in <s>piṇḍa</s> and water-offerings.
When the marriage has been performed,
on the fourth night,
she becomes one with her husband
in <s>piṇḍa</s>, <s>gotra</s>, and birth-impurity.
On the first day, or the second,
or the third or the fourth,
the collection of bones should be performed
by kinsmen with benevolent intent.
On the fourth, the fifth,
the seventh, and likewise the ninth,
bone-collection is prescribed
for the <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) in order.
On the eleventh day after death,
for the deceased for whom a bull is released,
he is freed from the world of the dead
and is honored in the heavenly world.
He whose bones float
in the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the doer of auspicious deeds,
for him there is no return
from the world of <s>Brahman</s>, by any means.
As long as the bones of human beings
remain in the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
for that many thousands of years
one is honored in the heavenly world.
Standing in water up to the navel,
one should contemplate in the heart:
"May my ancestors come,
may they accept these water-offerings."
Having joined both hands together,
and having filled them with water,
lifting up an amount equal to a cow's horn,
one should release the water into the water.
One should cast water into the sky,
standing in water, facing south.
The abode of the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors) is the sky,
and likewise the southern direction.
The waters are declared to be the host of gods;
the waters are likewise the host of ancestors.
Therefore, one who desires the welfare of the ancestors
should offer water-libations in water.
By day, heated by the rays of the sun;
by night, by the stars and the wind;
and at both twilights,
water is always pure.
Naturally endowed and not contaminated
by impurity, always pure,
whether stored in a vessel or resting on the ground,
water is always pure.
For the gods and for the ancestors,
one should offer water-libations in water.
For those who died without sacraments,
one should offer water-libations on dry ground.
At the <s>śrāddha</s> and at the time of oblation,
one should give with one hand.
With both hands one should give at <s>tarpaṇa</s> (water-libation);
thus is the <s>dharma</s> established.
Thus ends the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (law treatise) composed by <s>Yama</s>.
This <s>Yamasmṛti</s> is concluded.
